title: Captain America
edition: the 1979 television pilot starring Reb Brown as Steve Rogers

sources.label: Reactor retrospective on both television films

synopsis: Steve hopes to travel and draw after military service. An experimental serum saves him after a crash. Two hostages give him a reason to use his new strength.
verdictRationale: Steve chooses to enter alone because a show of force could cost Tina and Dr. Day their lives. Their safety guides his choice before he puts on the costume. Brackett exploits Tina’s desire to clear her father’s name. The rescue shows the difference between earning trust and abusing it.
ageRationale: Steve is badly injured in a crash. Two women are held at gunpoint, and the bomb threatens people outside the immediate fight. Children may need help understanding why the adults hesitate to rush in.
reflection: Mills can outfit Steve for a rescue, but the costume cannot tell him whose needs come first. His most thoughtful decision comes when he considers what the hostages will face once he walks through the door.

themes.name: Prudence
themes.evidence: Steve argues for a smaller rescue because a larger intervention endangers the captives. His judgment shapes the mission.

references.label: Reactor retrospective on both television films

themes.name: Service
themes.evidence: After freeing the women, Steve continues to pursue the truck. His willingness to protect people he has never met drives the climax.

themes.evidence: Brackett claims he can clear Tina’s father and then takes her captive. Exploiting her trust enables his scheme.

title: Captain America II: Death Too Soon
edition: the two-part CBS sequel starring Reb Brown and Christopher Lee, broadcast November 23–24, 1979

sources.label: Reactor retrospective on both television films

synopsis: Steve helps an older woman whose neighbors have been robbed. His next investigation leads him to a town whose residents depend on treatment controlled by the man who made them ill.
verdictRationale: Steve makes time to hear Mrs. Shaw’s account of the stolen checks. Later, Helen’s explanation helps him understand why an entire town has kept quiet. His willingness to listen matters to the rescue. Miguel’s hold over the town shows the cruelty of making care conditional on obedience.
ageRationale: People age against their will and fear losing treatment. Dogs threaten Steve during the rescue. The loss of control over one’s body may particularly trouble children worried about an older relative.
reflection: A frightened neighbor can appear uncooperative while protecting people who have been threatened. Helen’s disclosure gives Steve both knowledge and an obligation to use it for people who cannot speak safely.

themes.name: Care for vulnerable neighbors
themes.evidence: Steve responds to the thefts Mrs. Shaw describes and helps bring the antidote to Portland. Protection connects the opening encounter to the ending.

references.label: Reactor retrospective on both television films

themes.name: Courage in telling the truth
themes.evidence: Helen explains how Miguel keeps the town compliant. One disclosure changes what Steve understands about the residents’ silence.
